subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum witnessed the death of a two-headed stone giant at the hands of Duergar using a magical flame device, observed Thorin’s attempt to subdue it, noted Daz’s deliberate weakening of his spells, and heard Zalthir’s fists and Thorin’s blade striking the giant — ultimately rushing in to strike with his mace. He watched Thorin mourn the giant and saw the Duergar shrink to standard size after the giant’s death.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue the two-headed stone giant, pleaded with the Duergar not to kill it, and later prayed for the dead. He inquired about unusual behavior among giants, used a precise definition of anti-social, non-profitable madness to communicate with the Duergar, and was directed by Dorhun — a stone giant apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam — to visit Cairngorm Cavern. He confirmed that he tried to subdue Hgraam, not kill him, and was granted safe passage by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: “Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him,” shouts Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was focused on survival against being burned, crushed, or arrested. He encountered Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for a service. Gartokkar revealed the city’s use of a fire dragon to fuel furnaces, misunderstood sarcasm about being a ‘lighter,’ and laughed at Grygum’s joke about kindling. Zalthir was warned the offer expires tomorrow and that future encounters may not be friendly.
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast magic that deliberately weakened the stone giant’s defenses, as observed by Grygum. He expressed amusement at Gartokkar’s description of the fire dragon as a ‘lighter,’ suppressing a snigger. He was intrigued by the mechanics of the dragon-fueled furnaces and the role of the Keepers of the Flame in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Daz ask while holding down a snigger, “So he’s a lighter?”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, responsible for tending Themberchaud — a fire dragon that burns stone-hot to fuel Gracklstugh’s furnaces. He is literal-minded, misunderstood sarcasm, laughed at a joke for the first time in long memory, and offered Zalthir safe passage through the city in exchange for a service. He warned that the offer expires tomorrow and that future interactions may be hostile if declined.
source_quote: “Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh. If you were to come to the Keepers of the Flame headquarters and do me a service, I could give you safe passage through the city.”

subject: Dorhun
fact: Dorhun is a stone giant and former apprentice to Stonespeaker Hgraam. He confirmed Thorin’s account of trying to subdue Hgraam, explained that stone giants have qualified immunity if rampaging, and invited Thorin to visit Cairngorm Cavern before leaving the city. He introduced Rihuud as his companion and commanded Stone Guards to grant Thorin passage, despite the Duergar’s visible resentment.
source_quote: “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?”

subject: Rihuud
fact: Rihuud is a stone giant and companion of Dorhun, also an apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam. He accompanied Dorhun when he met Thorin and was present when Dorhun granted passage through the city. He did not speak but was part of the authoritative presence that commanded the Stone Guards.
source_quote: “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.”

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a prestigious faction within Gracklstugh, responsible for tending Themberchaud — a fire dragon that burns stone-hot to fuel the city’s furnaces. They are among the Deepking’s most prized advisors. They use a magical flame device to control the dragon’s output and operate under the authority of the Custodian of the Flame. They value utility and efficiency, and they have the power to grant safe passage and immunity from imprisonment.
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are a faction of stone giants serving as enforcers or gatekeepers in Gracklstugh, loyal to their own kind and under the command of stone giants like Dorhun. They are distinct from Duergar authority and were ordered to grant Thorin passage despite Duergar disapproval, indicating their autonomy and higher status among the city’s non-Duergar powers.
source_quote: Turning to the Duergar with the stone weapons, he says, “Stone Guards, you are to let them through.”

subject: Duergar Patrol
fact: The Duergar patrol operates under the authority of the Deepking and is responsible for monitoring and suppressing anti-social, non-profitable madness among giants. They use magical flame devices to subdue or kill rogue stone giants. They are suspicious of non-Duergar authority, resentful of stone giants’ privileges, and maintain strict control over who enters or exits their city. They reported a recent surge in such incidents and acknowledged no known cause.
source_quote: “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.”

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Cairngorm Cavern is a location in Gracklstugh, referenced by Dorhun as a place Thorin must visit before leaving the city. It is implied to be a site of significance to stone giant lore, possibly tied to the legacy of Stonespeaker Hgraam and the deeper history of the city’s giants.
source_quote: “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a subterranean city ruled by the Deepking, where Duergar hold administrative power but stone giants retain ceremonial and military authority. The city relies on the Keepers of the Flame and their fire dragon, Themberchaud, to fuel its furnaces. It has prisons, militias, and a complex hierarchy where non-Duergar individuals require special permission to move freely. The city is marked by tension between Duergar control and stone giant autonomy.
source_quote: “Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh.”

subject: Flame Device
fact: The flame device is a magical apparatus used by Duergar to control and project fire, consisting of a tube connected to a bottle on the back, with a small external flame produced by a magic concoction lit when a lever is pulled. It was used to kill the two-headed stone giant and is a signature tool of the Duergar militias.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a fire dragon kept by the Keepers of the Flame in Gracklstugh. It burns stone-hot and is used to fuel the city’s furnaces, replacing the need for large amounts of kindling. It is a living, controlled weapon of industrial power, and its care is the most prized duty in the Deepking’s service.
source_quote: “we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.”

subject: death of the two-headed stone giant
fact: The two-headed stone giant was subdued by Thorin’s attempts and Daz’s weakening spells, struck by Zalthir and Grygum, and ultimately killed by a Duergar flame device. The event triggered Thorin’s mourning, Grygum’s intervention, and the Duergar’s subsequent shrinking to standard size, indicating the completion of their ritual or magical transformation.
source_quote: The Duergar, unconvinced by Thorin’s entreaties, kill the giant.

subject: shrinking of the Duergar
fact: After the death of the stone giant, the Duergar who used the flame device shrank to their standard size, suggesting their enlarged forms were magically sustained during the confrontation and were temporary. This shift was observed by Grygum and marked the end of the immediate threat.
source_quote: Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: mystery of the stone giant madness
fact: A surge of anti-social, non-profitable madness among stone giants has been reported by Duergar, with no known cause. This phenomenon has increased militia work and may be tied to a clan leader’s hidden knowledge. Thorin and Dorhun’s encounters suggest this is a systemic issue with deep roots in the city’s power structure.
source_quote: “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior... And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.”

subject: Gartokkar’s offer to Zalthir
fact: Gartokkar offered Zalthir safe passage and protection in Gracklstugh in exchange for a service, with the offer expiring tomorrow. Failure to accept may result in hostile future encounters. The nature of the service is unspecified, creating a pending plot thread that could lead Zalthir into the heart of the Keepers of the Flame’s operations.
source_quote: “The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.”

subject: Dorhun’s invitation to Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Dorhun invited Thorin to visit Cairngorm Cavern before leaving the city, implying that Hgraam’s legacy, the stone giants’ history, or a deeper secret lies there. This is an unresolved thread that may connect to the mystery of the giant madness, the Duergar’s control, or the origins of the fire dragon.
source_quote: “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The events described occurred on the 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, marking the temporal anchor for the death of the stone giant, the Duergar’s shrinking, Thorin’s encounter with Dorhun, and the expiration of Gartokkar’s offer.
source_quote: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a traveler who seeks to understand the power dynamics of the Underdark, particularly regarding the Keepers of the Flame, the Red Dragon, and the Duergar regime. He is cautious about aligning with factions and values information over commitment.
source_quote: Daz wonders if they should interview the various factions to find out which one they should join or whether they should join any of them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc who sneaks peeks to gather intelligence, speaks with pragmatic humor, and is perceived as non-threatening despite his appearance. He is trusted by Daz as a companion in navigating dangerous social terrain.
source_quote: Grygum, who sneaks a quick peek, says that inside is a pretty dour place where people talk only in hushed whispers.

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling is an outsider in the Underdark who survives by appearing harmless, avoiding political entanglements, and sharing information with those not 'in the game.' He is well-informed about factional conflicts, the Deepking’s madness, and the Keepers of the Flame’s predicament.
source_quote: I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow is from Menzoberranzan and views Duergar violence as crude and artless compared to the refined politicking of his homeland. He is disgusted by the lack of style in Duergar conflict and contrasts their brutality with the elegance of drow intrigue.
source_quote: The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is the captain of the Stone Guards on the lake, commanding authority through stern presence. She seeks covert assistance to locate the rogue Duergar Droki without provoking war with the Derro, and she navigates diplomacy with a mix of threat and charm.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a traveler who is tempted to join the Stone Guards but is wary of factional entanglements. He is influenced by the halfling’s warnings and struggles to distinguish between helping the guards and serving the city’s interests.
source_quote: Are we helping you? Or the city?

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a powerful Duergar organization that controls the Red Dragon, providing it with a horde and pampering it to ensure its cooperation in maintaining the city’s furnaces. They are in a precarious position, as the dragon grows more powerful and resentful, and they must periodically kill and replace it. They are also threatened by the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.
source_quote: The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him. The problem... is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle. And so, at some point, the Dragon discovers it’s not in charge. Then, the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a hostile faction opposing the Keepers of the Flame, likely a shadowy group of insurgents or assassins. They are in conflict with the Crown and are a threat to the stability of the Duergar regime.
source_quote: They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: The Crown
fact: The Crown is a rival power to the Keepers of the Flame, possibly a royalist or centralized authority seeking to reclaim control over the Duergar city. It is in open conflict with both the Keepers and the Gray Ghosts.
source_quote: They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are the official law enforcement of the city, loyal to the Duergar regime and operating from the Overlake Hold. They are pragmatic, austere, and prefer covert operations to avoid open conflict, especially with the Derro.
source_quote: I am Errde Blackskull, captain of the Stone Guards on the lake, and I must ask that you come to my office so we can talk.

subject: Duergar Regime
fact: The Duergar regime is characterized by brutal efficiency, arbitrary laws under the Deepking, and a complete absence of art or ceremony in governance. It is in decline, as its leaders are detached from reality and its institutions are increasingly unstable.
source_quote: Now, they don’t. It’s as if he is detached from reality.

subject: Red Dragon’s periodic replacement
fact: The Keepers of the Flame must regularly kill and replace the Red Dragon that powers the city’s furnaces, due to the dragon’s growing power and resentment of subordination. Dragon eggs are purchasable and hatchable, enabling this cycle.
source_quote: So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.

subject: Droki’s disappearance
fact: Droki, a rogue Duergar residing in the West Cleft District among the Derro, has evaded capture. His whereabouts and motives are unknown, but his presence threatens to provoke war if the Stone Guards move against him directly.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.

subject: Deepking’s madness
fact: The Deepking’s rule has become increasingly arbitrary and detached from reality, leading to the collapse of logical law in Gracklstugh. This madness is the root cause of current factional instability and the Keepers of the Flame’s desperation.
source_quote: It all began with the Deepking’s madness.

subject: Not relevant to the game
fact: The phrase 'Not relevant to the game' has emerged as a cryptic mantra among outsiders who avoid factional entanglements. It defines a survival philosophy in the Underdark, separating observers from participants.
source_quote: What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.

subject: Darklake Brewery
fact: The Darklake Brewery is a closed establishment, accessible only to Duergar. It is a place of hushed conversations and covert information exchange, located just outside the Blade Bazaar. It is the site of key encounters with the halfling, Drow, and the Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Brewery is closed to non-Duergar, and Daz is disappointed until Grygum, who sneaks a quick peek, says that inside is a pretty dour place where people talk only in hushed whispers.

subject: Overlake Hold
fact: The Overlake Hold is the austere guardhouse and administrative center of the Stone Guards. Made entirely of grey stone, it reflects the cold, brutal efficiency of Duergar governance. It is where Errde Blackskull conducts official business and recruits covert agents.
source_quote: A few minutes later, they are in the Overlake Hold, the local guard house. Errde brings them to a sitting room. Like everything in this town, it is austere. The chairs and table are made of stone. There is no color—the light is grey.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: The West Cleft District is a dangerous neighborhood inhabited by the Derro. It is the suspected hideout of the rogue Duergar Droki and is considered too volatile for direct military incursion by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.

subject: Dragon eggs
fact: Dragon eggs are available for purchase and can be hatched, enabling the Keepers of the Flame to replace the Red Dragon when necessary. This knowledge informs Daz’s understanding of the cycle of control and violence in the city.
source_quote: Daz wonders... how Dragon eggs can be purchased and hatched.

subject: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The events occur on the 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, a time of escalating tension in Gracklstugh as the Deepking’s madness destabilizes the regime and factions vie for power.
source_quote: [Continuing — Date: 9th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493, Speaker: Daz]

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is the guardian of the city against corruption, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly the Clan Lairds, and holds the key to uncovering the conspiracy centered on Droki. She can guarantee freedom and safe passage in exchange for Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: It is my job to protect the city from corruption. So yes, it is for the city.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is the central figure in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly elements of the Clan Lairds. His discovery is essential to proving the conspiracy.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognizes corruption through the lens of the Blade Bazaar, having witnessed and replicated its behaviors — grift, chaos, and rule-breaking — and identifies systemic corruption in authoritarian structures.
source_quote: Yes, there was much of that going on.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is implicated in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, with Droki linked to its activities and possibly complicit in undermining its rules.
source_quote: He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Clan Lairds
fact: The Clan Lairds are suspected of involvement in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, with Droki possibly tied to their clandestine operations.
source_quote: He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: escaped slaves
fact: A group of Drow may be searching for escaped slaves; Errde can deny their presence in the city, and her ability to provide this cover is a leverage point for Thorin’s freedom.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: corruption escalation
fact: Corruption began with rule-breaking in the bazaar, escalated to grift, then chaos, and now threatens destruction, as described by Errde and confirmed by Daz’s observations.
source_quote: Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment from the armory as a reward for initial cooperation, with another 175 gold pieces contingent on delivering Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: the city
fact: The city is the primary domain of the corruption, with the Deepking’s court at its heart, and Errde asserts her role as its protector against internal decay.
source_quote: There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court.

subject: proof of corruption
fact: Errde claims Daz’s description of the Blade Bazaar’s behaviors constitutes proof of corruption, linking systemic lawlessness in commerce to political decay.
source_quote: You have found me proof!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is seeking clarity on whether to align with the Stone Guards or the City, and is being manipulated by Errde’s promises of freedom and rewards in exchange for action against Droki.
source_quote: Look, we want to know if this is for the Stone Guards or the City?
